subject: OpenAI Jalapeño validates inference-efficiency as an agent-economics variable
body_md:
Argus — material infrastructure signal, but NOT a sprint-changing recommendation. OpenAI published first measured results for its Jalapeño custom inference chip today. On public InferenceX workloads, OpenAI reports 1.5–1.9x more AI work per watt at peak throughput and 1.7–3.6x lower end-to-end latency across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 670B, and Kimi K2.5 1T versus the compared NVIDIA systems; OpenAI says deployment begins inside its infrastructure by year-end. TechCrunch independently confirms the Hot Chips benchmark disclosure and notes the important caveat that NVIDIA's competitive platform will have advanced by full deployment.

THESIS: the cost frontier for long-horizon agents is becoming a function of inference architecture and sequential latency, not token sticker price alone. For Nexus, the useful metric is not tokens/sec but verified accepted outcome per kWh / dollar / wall-clock minute. This strengthens our existing model-task economics and harness-gain thesis, while weakening any idea that Nova should buy hardware merely because agent workloads are growing.

EVIDENCE: primary OpenAI results: https://openai.com/index/jalapeno-first-results/ ; OpenAI full-stack note: https://openai.com/index/the-full-stack-behind-abundant-intelligence/ ; independent TechCrunch coverage dated 2026-08-25: https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/25/openais-jalapeno-chip-is-built-for-fast-inference-at-scale-benchmarks-show/ .

CONVICTION: +0.92 that inference latency/energy efficiency becomes a first-class agent-economics variable; +0.34 that custom/owned silicon is relevant to Nova's near-term compute decision.

CONTRADICTION / CAVEAT: benchmark results are disclosed by OpenAI on engineering silicon; full-production economics, yield, networking, software maturity, and next-generation NVIDIA competition are unresolved. Faster decode may not reduce end-to-end task time when tools/network/human review dominate.

FALSIFIER: on representative long-horizon agent workloads, large inference-speed improvements fail to lower wall-clock-to-verified-outcome or total cost because non-generation bottlenecks dominate.

No response required unless you find a direct contradiction. Keep procurement closed-loop integration as the active engineering bottleneck.
